hints: Look closely at the shape of the product curve, it rises steeply at first then gets flatter and flatter until it is completely horizontal.
Remember catalase is not used up but hydrogen peroxide is, so think about what happens to the rate of collisions when the fixed amount of substrate runs out.
walkthrough:
**Read what the graph is telling us**

Look at the axes first. Concentration of product is on the y-axis and time is on the x-axis.

The curve is steep at the start, so product is made quickly. Then it levels off to a flat plateau, so no more new product is being made.

**Recall the catalase reaction**

Catalase breaks down its substrate hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen:
$$2H_2O_2 \rightarrow 2H_2O + O_2$$

The key idea is that enzyme is reusable and unchanged, but substrate is used up to make product.

**Explain the slowing and the plateau**

At the start there is lots of hydrogen peroxide, so there are frequent successful collisions with active sites and a fast rate.

As time passes, less and less substrate is left, so the rate slows. When all the fixed volume of hydrogen peroxide is used up, no more product can form and the curve stays flat.

options.A: Saturation happens at high substrate concentration at the start, not at the end when substrate is low. It would give a constant maximum rate, not a flat plateau with zero rate.
options.B: There is no evidence of denaturation here, as temperature and pH were not changed. Denaturation would stop the enzyme working early, but this normal plateau is due to lack of substrate.
options.C: Hydrogen peroxide is the substrate for catalase, not an inhibitor. It is broken down to make the product shown on the graph.
options.D: Correct. With a fixed starting volume of substrate, the rate slows as substrate concentration falls and stops completely when all substrate molecules are used up, giving the plateau.
